requirements.quote:
A sender SHOULD send a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame (type=0x16 or 0x17) when
   it wishes to open a stream but is unable to do so due to the maximum
   stream limit set by its peer; see Section 19.11.  A STREAMS_BLOCKED
requirements.condition: The sender wishes to open a stream but cannot because of the maximum stream limit set by its peer.
requirements.required_behavior: The sender should send a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame with type 0x16 or 0x17.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can place the sender at the peer-established stream limit, attempt to open another stream, and observe whether a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame is emitted.

requirements.quote:
frame of type 0x16 is used to indicate reaching the bidirectional
   stream limit, and a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame of type 0x17 is used to
   indicate reaching the unidirectional stream limit.
requirements.condition: A STREAMS_BLOCKED frame indicates that the bidirectional stream limit has been reached.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded frame type can be compared with the directionality of the reached stream limit.

requirements.quote:
frame of type 0x16 is used to indicate reaching the bidirectional
   stream limit, and a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame of type 0x17 is used to
   indicate reaching the unidirectional stream limit.
requirements.condition: A STREAMS_BLOCKED frame indicates that the unidirectional stream limit has been reached.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded frame type can be compared with the directionality of the reached stream limit.

requirements.quote:
A STREAMS_BLOCKED frame does not open the stream, but informs the
   peer that a new stream was needed and the stream limit prevented the
   creation of the stream.
requirements.condition: A STREAMS_BLOCKED frame is sent or received.
requirements.required_behavior: It informs the peer that a new stream was needed and that the stream limit prevented its creation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Processing the frame as opening a stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-machine test can verify that sending or receiving this frame does not create or open a stream and that the frame conveys blocked-stream status.

requirements.condition: A STREAMS_BLOCKED frame is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: The frame contains, in order, a variable-length integer Type field with value 0x16 or 0x17 followed by a variable-length integer Maximum Streams field.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame wire representation can be parsed to verify field order, integer encoding, and the fixed allowed type range.

requirements.quote:
Maximum Streams:  A variable-length integer indicating the maximum
      number of streams allowed at the time the frame was sent.  This
requirements.required_behavior: Maximum Streams is encoded as a variable-length integer containing the maximum number of streams allowed at the time the frame is sent.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can compare the encoded Maximum Streams value and encoding form with the sender's active stream limit at transmission time.

requirements.quote:
value cannot exceed 2^60, as it is not possible to encode stream
      IDs larger than 2^62-1.  Receipt of a frame that encodes a larger
      stream ID MUST be treated as a connection error of type
      STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR or FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
requirements.required_behavior: The encoded value is at most 2^60.
requirements.why_checkable: The Maximum Streams integer can be decoded and checked against the inclusive upper bound 2^60.

requirements.quote:
value cannot exceed 2^60, as it is not possible to encode stream
      IDs larger than 2^62-1.  Receipt of a frame that encodes a larger
      stream ID MUST be treated as a connection error of type
      STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR or FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
requirements.condition: A frame encoding a value larger than the permitted limit is received.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accepting or continuing normal processing of the invalid frame without the required connection error.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR or FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoder can be given an over-limit encoded value and the resulting connection error type can be observed.
